perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, he has access to the following information:

- Harold is a project manager. Arthur Begum is a police officer and a friend; Harold often relies on Arthur for advice and support.
- Harold felt frustrated and anxious that his project team was unmotivated and that this was affecting progress. He arranged to meet Arthur at a coffee shop and told Arthur he was at his wit’s end.
- Harold heard Arthur say motivation can be tricky, ask whether Harold had tried understanding what drives each team member individually, and suggest one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood on a personal level.
- Harold felt hopeful and relieved after the conversation and decided to implement Arthur’s suggestions in team meetings.
- Harold told his team he wanted quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them.
- Harold heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful, and Team Member 2 say they were open to it and wanted to see how it went.
- Harold said he would schedule time with each team member and work together to make the project a success.
- Later, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- Harold told Arthur he had tried the suggestions but the team still was not responding. He heard Arthur say there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold decided to set up another round of meetings to get to the bottom of the issue.
- Harold became determined and focused, believing there might be underlying team issues he had not addressed. He held one-on-one meetings and asked team members to share concerns or problems.
- Harold heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few team members that was affecting work. Harold said he would look into resolving the conflicts.
- Harold heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by the workload, found it hard to stay motivated, and were constantly stressed. Harold said he would see if tasks could be redistributed and that their well-being was important.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve team performance. He intended to create a more supportive, open team environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- Harold told the team about these changes. He heard Team Member 1 say it sounded great and would help them work better together, and Team Member 2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed.
- Harold said he was glad, that they should work together to make the project a success, and that their input and well-being were crucial to success.
